## The question and exact quadratic form

Let \(H=(\mathbb C^d)^{\otimes n}\), where \(d\ge3\). Identify \(C\in\operatorname{End}(H)\) with its vectorization across the two parties and put
\[
 Q_n(C)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}(-1/2)^{|S|}\|\operatorname{Tr}_S C\|_F^2.
\]
The endpoint Werner state \(\rho_d=(2I-F)/(2d^2-d)\) is positive and NPT for \(d>2\), and
\[
 \langle\operatorname{vec}(C),(\rho_d^\Gamma)^{\otimes n}\operatorname{vec}(C)\rangle
  =\big(2/(2d^2-d)\big)^n Q_n(C).
\]
Thus all-copy nondistillability of this particular state requires \(Q_n(C)\ge0\) for **every** \(n\) and **every complex rank-at-most-two** \(C\). This requirement remains open; the results below do not settle it.

For local matrix units \(E_{ij}\), the polarized quadratic form satisfies
\[
 B_n(E_{a b},E_{c e})=\prod_{r=1}^n\left(\delta_{a_r c_r}\delta_{b_r e_r}-\tfrac12\delta_{a_r b_r}\delta_{c_r e_r}\right),\quad Q_n(C)=B_n(C,C),
\]
with \(B_n\) conjugate-linear in its first variable.

## Theorem 1: exact local support-overlap test

Fix nonzero subspaces \(U_i,V_i\subseteq\mathbb C^d\), with orthogonal projections \(P_i,R_i\), and let \(\mathcal C\) be all operators \(C\) whose range lies in \(\bigotimes_i U_i\) and whose adjoint range lies in \(\bigotimes_i V_i\). Then
\[
 Q_n(C)\ge0\quad \text{for every }C\in\mathcal C
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Tr}(P_iR_i)\le2 \quad\text{for each }i.
\]
**Proof.** In vectorized coordinates, the one-site Hermitian operator for \(Q_1\) is \(K=I-\tfrac12|\Omega_d\rangle\langle\Omega_d|\), where \(|\Omega_d\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^d|jj\rangle\) is unnormalized. Its compression to \(U_i\otimes\overline{V_i}\) is \(I-\tfrac12|\eta_i\rangle\langle\eta_i|\), where \(\eta_i=(P_i\otimes\overline{R_i})\Omega_d\) and \(\|\eta_i\|^2=\operatorname{Tr}(P_iR_i)\). The full compressed operator, after permuting slots, is the tensor product of these local compressions. Each factor is positive semidefinite exactly when its overlap is at most two, proving sufficiency. If an overlap exceeds two, its local compression has a strictly negative eigenvalue. Every other local compression has a strictly positive eigenvalue (on a space of dimension one this follows from \(\operatorname{Tr}(P_iR_i)\le1\); otherwise it has an eigenvalue one). ## Theorem 2: second-order stability of the canonical zero witnesses

Let \(n\ge2\) be even, \(d\ge3\), \(a=0^n\), \(b=1^n\), and
\[
 C_0=|a\rangle\langle a|-|b\rangle\langle b|.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{rank}(C_0)=2\), \(Q_n(C_0)=0\). For **every twice differentiable path** \(C(t)\) of rank-at-most-two complex matrices with \(C(0)=C_0\),
\[
 Q_n(C(t))=t^2 H+o(t^2)\quad\text{with } H\ge0.
\]
The assertion is only second-order: it does not say \(Q_n\) is nonnegative in a neighborhood of \(C_0\).

**Proof.** Write \(P=\operatorname{span}(a,b)\) and \(J=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) on \(P\). Since \(PC_0P=J\) is invertible, every nearby rank-two matrix has a block-Schur parameterization
\[
 C(t)=(I+X(t))M(t)(I+Y(t))^*,
\]
where \(M(t):P\to P\), \(X(t),Y(t):P\to P^\perp\), \(M(0)=J\), \(X(0)=Y(0)=0\). Indeed, the invertible upper-left \(2\times2\) block determines the lower-right block by the rank-two Schur identity. Put \(M(t)=J+tM_1+O(t^2)\), \(X(t)a=t x+O(t^2)\), \(X(t)b=t z+O(t^2)\), \(Y(t)a=t y+O(t^2)\), \(Y(t)b=t w+O(t^2)\), with \(x,y,z,w\perp P\). The first-order term is
\[
 T=M_1+xa^*+ay^*-zb^*-bw^*.
\]
The second-order term has, modulo terms inside \(P\times P\) or off its diagonal blocks, the component \(xy^*-zw^*\). All the omitted terms are \(B_n\)-orthogonal to \(C_0\). Directly from the matrix-unit formula, \(B_n(C_0,C_0)=0\), \(B_n(C_0,T)=0\); hence
\[
 H=Q_n(T)+2\operatorname{Re}B_n(C_0,xy^*-zw^*).
\]
For each string \(c\notin\{a,b\}\), define \(m_0(c)=\#\{i:c_i=0\}\), \(m_1(c)=\#\{i:c_i=1\}\),
\[
 \alpha_c=2^{-m_0(c)},\quad\beta_c=2^{-m_1(c)},\quad
 A_c=\prod_i(\mathbf1_{c_i=0}-\tfrac12)-\prod_i(\mathbf1_{c_i=1}-\tfrac12).
\]
Let \(\mathcal B=\{0,1\}^n\setminus\{a,b\}\), and let \(\mathcal D\) be the remaining strings, i.e., those containing a symbol other than zero or one. For \(c\in\mathcal B\) set \(\bar c=(1-c_1,\ldots,1-c_n)\), \(\sigma_c=(-1)^{m_0(c)}\). Matrix-unit multiplication gives the **exact** decomposition
\[
\begin{split}
 H={}&2^{-n}|(M_1)_{aa}+(M_1)_{bb}|^2+|(M_1)_{ab}|^2+|(M_1)_{ba}|^2\\
 &+\sum_{c\in\mathcal B}\alpha_c\left(|x_c-\sigma_c\overline{w_{\bar c}}|^2+|y_c-\sigma_c\overline{z_{\bar c}}|^2\right)\\
 &+\sum_{c\in\mathcal D}\Big[\alpha_c(|x_c|^2+|y_c|^2)+2A_c\operatorname{Re}(x_c\overline{y_c})\\
 &\hspace{35mm}+\beta_c(|z_c|^2+|w_c|^2)-2A_c\operatorname{Re}(z_c\overline{w_c})\Big].
\end{split}
\]
